title: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
seo_title: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes Class 12 Chemistry Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 6)
standard_code: Class 12 Chemistry, Chapter 6: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
standard_text: Haloalkanes: nomenclature, nature of C–X bond, physical and chemical properties, optical rotation, mechanism of substitution reactions. Haloarenes: nature of C–X bond, substitution reactions (directive influence of halogen in monosubstituted compounds only). Uses and environmental effects of dichloromethane, trichloromethane, tetrachloromethane, iodoform, freons, DDT.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: naming and classifying halides, SN1 and SN2, elimination, optical activity, named reactions and environmental effects. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

Haloalkanes are named as halo-substituted alkanes and classed as 1°, 2° or 3° by the carbon bearing the halogen. Primary halides react mainly by SN2 (one step, inversion of configuration); tertiary halides by SN1 (via a carbocation, racemisation). Alcoholic KOH causes elimination following Saytzeff's rule.

Aryl halides react slowly in nucleophilic substitution because resonance gives the C–X bond partial double-bond character, but they undergo electrophilic substitution at ortho and para positions. Freons damage the ozone layer and DDT builds up in food chains.

Example

2-Bromobutane is?

Br on a carbon with two C

Answer: secondary

Example

NaI in acetone with R–Cl?

halogen exchange

Answer: Finkelstein reaction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking SN2 gives racemisation.
  • Saying aryl halides react like alkyl halides.
  • Mixing up Wurtz and Wurtz–Fittig.

faq.q: Why do tertiary haloalkanes react by S<sub>N</sub>1?
faq.a: They form stable tertiary carbocations, and their crowded carbon blocks back-side attack.
In the stratosphere they release chlorine radicals that destroy ozone.
